question.problem:
Which of the following integrals evaluates to zero due to symmetry?

I. ${\int }_{-5}^{5}3{x}^{7}\,\text{d}x$

II. ${\int }_{-3}^{3}{e}^{2x}\,\text{d}x$

III. ${\int }_{-1}^{1}\frac{2}{x-2}\,\text{d}x$
question.worked_solution:
Recall the following:

- a function $f(x)$ is *even* if $f(-x)=f(x)$

- a function $f(x)$ is *odd* if $f(-x)=-f(x)$

Moreover, for any odd function $f(x),$ the graph of $y=f(x)$ has rotational symmetry of order $2$ about the origin, so we have

$$
{\int }_{-a}^{a}f(x)\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

So, to determine which integrals evaluate to $0$ due to symmetry, we have to determine which integrands are odd functions.

- The function $f(x)=3{x}^{7}$ is an odd function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(-x) & =3(-x)^{7} \\  & =3(-{x}^{7}) \\  & =-3{x}^{7} \\  & =-f(x)\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by symmetry, we can conclude that

$$
{\int }_{-5}^{5}3{x}^{7}\,\text{d}x=0.
$$

- The function $g(x)={e}^{2x}$ is *not* an odd function:

$$
\begin{aligned}g(-x) & ={e}^{2(-x)} \\  & ={e}^{-2x} \\  & \ne -g(x)\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- The function $h(x)=\frac{2}{x-2}$ is *not* an odd function:

$$
\begin{aligned}h(-x) & =\frac{2}{(-x)-2} \\  & =\frac{2}{-x-2} \\  & =-\frac{2}{x+2} \\  & \ne -h(x)\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the correct answer is "I only."
